messages:
alex: :rotating_light: seeing a sustained increase in 429s at the API gateway and a correlated spike in KV cache stall logs from the serving layer. Trend started ~06:20 UTC. Traffic pattern looks like many distinct API keys + rapidly rotating UA strings and TLS JA3 variations. Not a single big customer.

maria: logs? any specific endpoints?

sre_lead: paste the grafana panel?

alex: pasting samples, high QPS to /v1/embeddings.batch and /v1/generate, but 429s also on token endpoints. snippet of access pattern: `api_key=redacted_*/ua=python-requests/ja3=78ab...` repeated with tiny bursts from many IPs.

infra-bot: Incident created: INC-2026-2183 — high-429-rate on apigw. Severity: P2. Auto-escalation to oncall.

oncall-bot: Paging @sre_lead (on-call rotation).

sre_lead: I see the KV cache ops latency graph — memcached miss+slowset spikes at the same time. Could be cache thrashing due to scrape fanout. Preliminary cause: high fanout + lots of small keys => degraded cache performance -> upstream requests queue up -> rate limiter tripping.

alex: agree. Attack looks low-and-slow scraping with rotated headers to bypass simple UA blocks. They are hitting batch embeddings which causes heavy CPU + large KV key churn.

sec_ops: WAF logs show a cluster of IPs with similar behavioral fingerprinting but changing UA/TLS. Need to add a behavioral rate-slice rule rather than static UA block.

maria: proposed live mitigations: 1) apply adaptive per-api-key rate-slices (limit concurrent requests + token rate) 2) disable embeddings.batch for unauthenticated/low-trust keys 3) add a WAF synthetic fingerprint rule to block the recurring JA3 set 4) increase KV cache TTL for hot prefixes to reduce churn.

sre_lead: priority order: (A) quick rate-slice via edge -> immediate QPS reduction, (B) disable embeddings.batch for keys with suspicious fingerprint, (C) tune cache TTLs, (D) WAF rule after small test window.

alex: executing (A). Pushing rate-slice rule to apigateway now:```bash
# rate-slice: limit to 4 req/s per key for endpoints /v1/embeddings.batch,/v1/generate
curl -X POST https://apigw-admin/_rules -H "Authorization: Bearer $ADMIN" -d '{"rule":"path:(/v1/embeddings.batch|/v1/generate) => per_key_rate(4rps)"}'
```

infra-bot: Rule deployed to edge region us-east-1 (staged to 50% edge) — deployment id: deploy-9832. Rolling to 100% in 60s.

sre_lead: monitoring 10s windows. watch 429 rate and 95th latency.

(60s later)

alex: 429s down ~42%. KV stall metric improving but still above baseline. QPS dropped ~35% overall.

sec_ops: starting controlled WAF fingerprint test: block list for JA3 hash `78ab...ef`. Will monitor false positives for 5m.

product-ops: support/customer comms note: potential degraded experience for high-volume batch embedding jobs while we mitigate abuse. Any customers impacted we should notify.

support_lead: will assemble a short triage note for affected customers and a templated status update. Keep me looped for list of keys we disable.

alex: (B) disabling embeddings.batch for keys flagged as low-trust via threat-score>70. Command:```json
{"action":"disable","endpoint":"/v1/embeddings.batch","condition":"threat_score>70"}
```

infra-bot: embedding endpoint disabled for 412 keys matching condition across regions.

maria: also bumped KV hot-prefix TTL from 30s -> 300s for candidate prefixes: `kv:prefix:emb:*`. This reduces churn and lowers set rate.

sre_lead: KV set latency dropping, downstream CPU for model hosts normalizing. 429s further down to ~60% reduction vs peak. Good.

sec_ops: WAF fingerprint block caused ~0.8% legitimate traffic hit initially — false positives minimal. Keeping rule active. If any legit customer reports, we can whitelist.

product-ops: heads up to legal/compliance: if we auto-disable features for customer keys we need a log entry and TTL for auto-reenable. Proposed: reenable after 24h and require human review.

support_lead: collecting list of accounts that lost embeddings.batch and drafting outbound: short explanation + ETA for re-enable + link to support form.

alex: handing off to night on-call. @sre_lead take the remainder? I'll paste final mitigation summary in thread. :white_check_mark:

sre_lead: taking handoff. Current state summary: rate-slice at edge (4rps per key) active globally, embeddings.batch disabled for flagged keys (412 total), WAF JA3 block active, KV TTL increased for hot prefixes. System health: 95th latency ~1.3x baseline; error rate trending down. Next actions: monitor for false-pos, implement whitelist mechanism, write a regression test for KV cache churn.

oncall-bot: Handoff accepted by @sre_lead. Reminder: next oncall shift at 23:00 UTC.

support_lead: sent initial customer notices to 12 high-usage accounts. Template used: "We detected abusive traffic patterns affecting embeddings.batch calls on your API key; we temporarily scoped batch embeddings for your key while we remediate. We anticipate restoration within 24 hours; contact support if you believe this is in error."

maria: adding metric alarms: if 429 rate <10% of peak for 30m, we run disable->re-enable candidate flow to gradually return service. Otherwise keep mitigations.

sec_ops: raising follow-up: we should add JA3 + behavioral clustering to our abuse detection pipeline to catch rotating-fingerprint scrapers earlier. Filing ticket: ABUSE-467.

product-ops: schedule post-incident review for tomorrow 14:00 UTC. Include SRE, SecOps, Product, Support. Want concrete remediation tasks and customer comms plan.

sre_lead: ack. leaving monitoring playbook and list of disabled keys in ops-docs. Will escalate to eng-runtime if KV metric regression reappears.

alex: thanks team. leaving thread for follow-up notes. :thumbsup:

(footnote) infra-bot: audit-log: actions taken - edge-rule deploy-9832, endpoint-disable batch-disable-412, waf-rule-id waf-2274, kv-ttl-change job-443. All actions logged to INC-2026-2183.
